sights.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1937 house for journalist Herbert Jacobs — often cited as his first Usonian design, and one of eight Wright buildings inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019. A private home: view from the street.

sights.address: 900 University Bay Dr, Shorewood Hills, WI 53705
sights.w: Wright's own congregation's church (1949–51), its copper-clad prow roof rising like hands in prayer — a National Historic Landmark (2004) with public tours.
UW–Madison's free art museum — 25,000 works across two buildings, the second a 2011 Machado-Silvetti addition — the second-largest collection in Wisconsin.

Madison's oldest Wright-designed house (1903), built for his boyhood friend 'Robie' Lamp and hidden inside a downtown block two streets from the Capitol — Atlas Obscura calls it an Easter egg. Exterior only.
The Badgers' 1917 stadium on a Civil War training-camp site — come for a home game and 'Jump Around' between the third and fourth quarters, when 76,000 people make the stands sway.

sights.address: E11376 Shady Lane Rd, Baraboo, WI 53913
sights.w: The world's only collection of all 15 crane species, at the Baraboo headquarters of the conservation group founded by two Cornell ornithology students in 1973 — Tone Madison calls it the nature scene's must-see.
The Ringling Brothers' winter quarters (1884–1918), now a Wisconsin Historical Society museum of circus wagons and history with summer big-top shows — a National Historic Landmark.

sights.address: 114 Shake Rag St, Mineral Point, WI 53565
sights.w: Restored 1840s stone and log cottages of Cornish lead miners on Mineral Point's Shake Rag Street, run as a Wisconsin Historical Society site — pair it with a Cornish pasty in town.
The highest point in southern Wisconsin: two observation towers atop the West Blue Mound look north to the Baraboo Range and east to Madison, with mountain-bike and hiking trails and a hilltop pool.

sights.address: Lakeshore Nature Preserve, Univ. Bay Dr entrance, Madison, WI 53705
sights.w: A wooded peninsula that juts nearly a mile into Lake Mendota inside UW's 300-acre Lakeshore Nature Preserve — a flat walk to fire circles at the tip with the Capitol skyline across the water. On the north shore, Atlas Obscura's never-opened 1968 'Wright-style' beach house.

sights.address: South bank of the Wisconsin River, northeast of Baraboo, WI
sights.w: The worn-out farm and converted chicken coop where Aldo Leopold's family replanted pines and prairie in the 1930s — the place that grew 'A Sand County Almanac'. A National Historic Landmark (2009); tours via the Aldo Leopold Foundation.
César Pelli's 2004 performing-arts center at the top of State Street — Overture Hall, the restored Capitol Theater and, next door, the Madison Museum of Contemporary Art.
